To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
clients value client-centred practice and the therapist's response is a key factor that can influence its application.
clients are able to articulate what they want from a therapeutic relationship and that they want to be listened to and understood.
clients value client-centeredness and want to participate in their own treatment, but are sometimes unable to do so because of the therapist, the illness or the treatment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a client-centred approach in mental health practice.
client-centred practice as a process of negotiation between the client and the therapist.
how clients' views can be used to inform practice in mental health services.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
client-centred practices are important to clients and should be applied to all client groups.
client-centredness is a complex and multi-dimensional concept that is influenced by a range of factors, including the client, the therapist and the context.
client-centred care is an important aspect of mental health care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clients' experience of the therapist's approach to client-centred practice is an important aspect of their recovery and should be a priority in mental health services.
client-centred care is a key factor for clients in the recovery process and that therapists can facilitate this process.
client-centredness is important to clients and that it should be an essential part of all mental health programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the client's experience of mental illness is central to client-centred practice, and therapists need to be aware of this in order to facilitate the client's recovery.
client-centred care can be facilitated by therapists and clients working together to negotiate the client's goals.

the therapist should take the time to understand the clients perspective and work with them to develop an individualized treatment plan that is consistent with the clients values, beliefs and goals for therapy.
